title: Morphisms from the spectrum of a field to an affine scheme: the image point and the residue field map
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. (1) For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-residue-field] is the residue field of $R_{\mathfrak p}$, and the composite $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ has kernel $\mathfrak p$ and makes $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ a fraction field of the domain $R/\mathfrak p$. (2) For a scheme $X$ and an affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $\mathcal O_X(U)=R$ (so $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$) and a point $x\in U$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$, the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ factors through $U$ and corresponds (on $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$) to the ring map $R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(x)$ of (1). (3) Let $K$ be a field, $\psi:R\to K$ a ring map, and $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ the induced morphism. Then $s$ maps the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to $\mathfrak q=\ker\psi$, and the field map $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$ induced by $s$ on residue fields is the unique ring map $\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak q)=\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$ extending the injection $R/\mathfrak q\to K$ induced by $\psi$. In particular, if $R$ is a domain, $\psi$ is injective and $K$ is a fraction field of $R$ via $\psi$, then $s$ maps the point to the generic point $(0)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\kappa((0))\to K$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: *Clause (1).* Let $\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)$ be the residue field of the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-residue-field] and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\pi:R\to R_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] there is an isomorphism $e:\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ under which the map $R=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak p}\to\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)$ becomes $\pi$; so the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ at $\mathfrak p$ is the residue field of $R_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (a) $\ker\pi=\mathfrak p$, and by (b) $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a field of fractions of the domain $R/\mathfrak p$ via the injection $R/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ induced by $\pi$.

proof.text: *Clause (2).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $x\in U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] there is an open immersion $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ with image $U$ (it identifies $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $U$) and a prime $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_x$ with $\iota_U(\mathfrak p)=x$. Write $j_z$ for the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to Z$ of a point $z$ of a scheme $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to $g=\iota_U$ at $\mathfrak p$: $\iota_U\circ j_{\mathfrak p}=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)$, where $r:\kappa(x)\to\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)$ is the map on residue fields, an isomorphism since $\iota_U$ is an open immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification], $j_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1}\circ\pi)$ with $e,\pi$ as in step 1. Composing with $\operatorname{Spec}(r^{-1})$ and using that $\operatorname{Spec}$ is a contravariant functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum]: $j_x=\iota_U\circ j_{\mathfrak p}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r^{-1})=\iota_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r^{-1}\circ e^{-1}\circ\pi)$. So $j_x$ factors through $\iota_U$, i.e. through $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, and the factorization is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the ring map $R\xrightarrow{\pi}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\kappa(x)$, the isomorphism being $r^{-1}\circ e^{-1}$: this is the identification $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(x)$ of the statement.

proof.text: *Clause (3), the point.* $K$ is a field, so its only prime ideal is $(0)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has one point $\xi=(0)$. By the description of $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ on points [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (Algebra 00E2: $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ maps a prime $\mathfrak q'$ to $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$), $s(\xi)=\psi^{-1}(0)=\ker\psi=\mathfrak q$; it is a prime ideal since $R/\mathfrak q$ embeds in the field $K$.

proof.text: *Clause (3), the residue field map.* Let $\varphi:\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak q)\to K$ be the map induced by $s$ on residue fields (from the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K,\xi}=K$). By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], $s=j_{\mathfrak q}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] $j_{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1}\circ\pi)$, with $e:\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ and $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. Put $\lambda=\varphi\circ e^{-1}:\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$ (this is the residue field map of $s$ read on $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ through $e$, step 1). By functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$, $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)=s=\operatorname{Spec}(\lambda\circ\pi)$, and since every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of exactly one ring map [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\psi=\lambda\circ\pi$. As $\pi$ induces the injection $R/\mathfrak q\hookrightarrow\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak q)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (a), (b)), $\lambda$ extends the injection $\bar\psi:R/\mathfrak q\to K$ induced by $\psi$. Any ring map $\lambda':\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to K$ extending $\bar\psi$ satisfies $\lambda'\circ\pi=\psi=\lambda\circ\pi$, hence $\lambda'=\lambda$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (c). So the residue field map is the unique extension of $\bar\psi$.

proof.text: *Clause (3), the generic case.* Let $R$ be a domain, $\psi$ injective and $K$ a fraction field of $R$ via $\psi$. Then $\mathfrak q=\ker\psi=(0)$ (step 3), and $(0)$ is the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$: it is contained in every prime, so every prime lies in its closure $V((0))=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (b) $\kappa((0))$ is a fraction field of $R$ via $\pi$, and by step 4 $\lambda:\kappa((0))\to K$ satisfies $\lambda\circ\pi=\psi$. $\lambda$ is injective, being a ring map out of a field into a nonzero ring. It is surjective: every $k\in K$ is $\psi(a)\psi(b)^{-1}$ with $a,b\in R$, $b\neq0$, and $\pi(b)\ne0$ since $\ker\pi=(0)$, so $k=\lambda(\pi(a)\pi(b)^{-1})$. Hence $\lambda$, and with it $\varphi=\lambda\circ e$, is an isomorphism.
